narrative.overview:
The page is a proof sheet: real captures of real projects laid out on warm grey paper, each one a print with a lit edge and a shadow falling right, and everything else is the annotation a reviewer writes beside them. The work is the evidence. Type, rules and colour exist to point at it, name it and get out of the way, so a recruiter scanning for half a minute sees running software before they read a sentence.

The system is Hallmark's Coral theme (warm paper, General Sans, one coral signal, physical sheet edges) disciplined by a technical register borrowed from Console: Geist Mono for anything measured or named in code (technology names, years, dates, figures, keys, API shapes), hairline rules between panels, and a dark mode that leans to warm graphite rather than black. Coral's felt desk, stationery props and desk animation are deliberately not used; the only pictures are captures and the projects' own figures.

Density is low and deliberate: one idea per screen, about 80 words in any 900px window, large type where a fact is the point, and generous air between sections earned by the mass of the pictures and lists they frame.
keyCharacteristics: Real captures as sheets: a cotton mat, a lit edge and one cast falling right; never a drawn browser or device frame.
One coral signal: the primary action, the current item, links on hover and the focus ring.
General Sans for everything read; Geist Mono only for what is measured or named in code.
Light and dark rendered from one token set: parity, never inversion.
Motion is small and physical: a settle on load, a 1 to 2px lift on hover, a press on click; reduced motion makes it instant.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Coral marks the primary action (Pressed Coral), the current or selected item and hover underlines (Deep Coral), and focus (Focus Coral), and nothing else: never a band, a fill behind running text or a heading colour.

rules.name: The No Side Bar Rule
rules.body: State is never a bar down one side of a row or box: use a tint, a full ring or an underline.

rules.name: The No Absolutes Rule
rules.body: No `#000` or `#fff` anywhere; every neutral carries a trace of hue 55.

rules.name: The Measured Mono Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono sets only what is named in code or measured (React Native, 2026, 97.07%, Ctrl K, JSON); prose, labels and headings are always General Sans.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No small tracked capitals above headings and no all-caps labels; a section opens with its head.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: There is one light, from the left: every shadow falls right, and no surface glows.

rules.name: The Dark Is Lightness Rule
rules.body: In dark mode no surface casts; it steps lighter or takes a hairline ring.

dos: **Do** frame every capture as a sheet: the 4px Cotton Mat, 8px radius, sheet edge and a cast falling right.
**Do** keep coral to the primary action (Pressed Coral), current and selected state and hover underlines (Deep Coral) and the focus ring (Focus Coral).
**Do** set technology names, years, dates, figures, keys and code in Geist Mono, and everything else in General Sans.
**Do** re-derive every colour for dark mode from its light value and keep the hue; step surfaces lighter instead of adding shadows.
**Do** keep any 900px window to about 80 words and the hero to a headline, one sentence and its actions.
**Do** give every interactive element hover, active, disabled and an instant 2px Focus Coral ring, and every animation a reduced-motion fallback.
donts: **Don't** draw browser bars, device frames or window chrome around captures.
**Don't** use Coral's felt desk, stationery props or photographs; the pictures are real captures and the projects' own figures only.
**Don't** use coral as a band, a heading colour or a fill behind running text.
**Don't** use pill buttons, tracked capitals, eyebrows or middle-dot meta strings.
**Don't** mark state with a bar down one side of a row or box.
**Don't** use `#000`, `#fff` or a cool grey anywhere.
**Don't** add a second light: no glows, no upward or left-falling shadows.
